A substantial article whose paragraphs are not paragraphs

The layout engine treats every block as a candidate for the reading column, and the decision about which blocks belong to the article is made before any of them are laid out. This paragraph exists to carry enough words that the page reads as substantial prose to a human, while being marked up with divs rather than paragraph elements.
Some publishers, particularly older CMS templates and a number of hand-rolled sites, wrap body copy in generic containers instead of semantic paragraph tags. The text is identical to a reader, and the rendered result is indistinguishable, but the document structure is not the one a heuristic keyed on paragraph elements expects to find.
A third block of prose, again long enough to clear any per-block minimum, so that the total word count of this page is unambiguously that of a real article rather than a listing page or an index of links to other articles elsewhere on the same site.
And a fourth, because the threshold under test is two hundred words of substantial prose and the page must sit well clear of it for the assertion to mean anything at all about the behaviour rather than about where exactly the boundary happens to fall today.
